newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: Czech PX50 continues surge led by major issues.
newsitem.headline: Czech PX50 continues surge led by major issues.

text.p: The Czech PX50 built on strong gains seen at the end of last week with blue chips, especially banking stocks, rising strongly.
The PX50 closed up six points on Monday to 563.9 while the RPIX gained 16 points to 563.9.
Major issues were all sharply up. Ceska Sporitelna rose 18 crowns to 338, Komercni Banka gained 52 crowns to 2,350, SPT Telecom was up 20 crowns to 3,330 and CEZ gained 11 crowns to 1,050.

Despite the strong performance of the blue chips, however, traders were sceptical that the pace of growth could be sustained, pointing to the traditional discrepancy between prices on the over-the-counter market and the Prague Stock Exchange (PSE).
"There is a big, big difference between prices on the OTC and on the (PSE) continuous trading," warned Ivan Kusacek of Zivnostenska Banka.
Kusacek said blue chip prices on the PSE, especially CEZ's, were nowhere near the market price on over-the-counter trading.
"There's no chance of 1,050 for CEZ on OTC trading. I would see roughly 1,030 for CEZ," he said.
Kusacek said the sharp gains to blue chips on Monday were caused mainly by investors "revaluing their portfolios" and said he expected most of the major issues to fall back a little on Tuesday.
Turnover, which was 3.4 billion crowns, was also likely to decline, he said.
